newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns Turkey about Libya, Sudan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns Turkey about Libya, Sudan.

text.p: The United States on Monday warned Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to be careful as he visits and seeks to engage Libya and the Sudan, two nations Washington considers state sponsors of terrorism.
"Our advice would be to be quite careful for any respected international leader to travel to those two countries to meet with their leadership," said State Department spokesman Nicholas BUrns.
"Be quite careful of these regimes and understand who they are, and what they have done to violate basic international norms," he added in response to a question at a news briefing.

He spoke as a team of Turkish trade officials headed for Libya on Monday ahead of Erbakan's visit this week to secure Tripoli's outstanding debts of up to $365 million to Turkish building contractors. There is also talk of Erbakan inviting Sudan's president to Turkey.

Few foreign leaders visited Tripoli since the United Nations slapped an air and limited trade embargo on Libya in 1991 for its refusal to hand over two Libyans suspected of blowing up a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland in 1988.
"We certainly would have concern about any country normalising relations with Sudan and Libya," BUrns said.

"Sudan is a state sponsor of terrorism. Libya is responsible for the murder of hundreds of Americans on Pam Am Flight 103, December 1989. And we haven't forgotten that. We know that the Libyans are harbouring two individuals who are responsible for that bombing," he added.

The spokesman said he did not know if the United States had formally told Turley of its reservations about Erbakan's dealings with Libya and Sudan but "I simply am taking the opportunity now, I think, to suggest what is commonsensical from an American government point of view."
